title: Silver Lake, Intel-Backed Altera Confidentially Files for U.S. IPO
gist: Altera, the FPGA maker Silver Lake took control of from Intel in 2025, has confidentially filed a Form S-1 for a U.S. IPO that Reuters says could raise more than $2 billion, giving both Silver Lake and Intel's residual 49% stake a monetization route. The 2025 deal valued Altera at $8.75 billion versus the roughly $16.7 billion Intel paid in 2015, and management guides to mid-20% revenue growth this year.

insights.claim: Altera's parent has submitted a draft Form S-1 registration statement to the SEC confidentially, with share count and price range still undetermined.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A confidential S-1 starts the SEC review clock, so a public flip of the filing is the next observable catalyst for pricing an FPGA comp set.

insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Investors should not expect comparable FPGA financials until the public flip; information asymmetry favors insiders in the interim.

insights.claim: Reuters has reported the Altera offering could raise more than $2 billion and could occur as early as this year, which would rank it among the largest semiconductor IPOs in recent years.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A $2B+ chip IPO absorbs sizeable dedicated semiconductor allocation and sets a sentiment marker for other AI-infrastructure listings.

insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The $8.75B mark is the reference valuation any IPO price will be measured against, and the implied step-up is the return Silver Lake is underwriting.

insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A concrete data point on Intel's M&A track record; it frames scepticism about valuations Intel assigns to other non-core assets it may divest.

insights.claim: Intel still owns 49% of Altera, so a successful listing creates a marked-to-market, liquefiable asset on Intel's balance sheet rather than an illiquid private stake.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Watch Intel's residual stake as a potential funding source for its capital-hungry foundry plans and as a sum-of-the-parts input.

insights.claim: Altera CEO Raghib Hussain said in July that the company expected revenue growth in the mid-20% range this year, a growth rate that underpins the IPO pitch.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Mid-20% growth is the number to test against the eventual public S-1; a shortfall would compress the multiple the deal can command.
insights.quote: the company expected revenue growth in the mid-20% range this year

insights.claim: Altera's FPGAs, which customers configure after manufacturing, sell into data centers, telecommunications networks, industrial machinery, AI systems, and aerospace and defense, giving it a diversified cyclical mix rather than pure AI exposure.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The end-market spread means the IPO is partly a bet on defense and industrial recovery, not only on AI data-center capex.

insights.claim: The filing is timed to a U.S. listings market regaining momentum and investor preference for companies tied to expanding AI infrastructure, meaning the deal depends on that window staying open.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Altera's pricing becomes a live read on how much AI-adjacent scarcity premium the primary market will still pay.
insights.quote: The filing comes as the U.S. listings market regains momentum and investors continue to favor companies tied to expanding AI infrastructure.
